responsibility: Defines rustc_target’s target ABI and type-layout model and uses it to lower function signatures for all supported architectures and foreign ABIs. The module’s core ABI layer exposes layout/index wrapper types, `TyAndLayout` traversal, and the `TyAbiInterface` that lets call lowering inspect Rust types, while the shared call framework defines `ArgAbi`/`FnAbi`, pass modes, argument attributes, register and cast representations, and dispatch to target-specific classifiers. The per-architecture call files then apply each platform’s calling-convention rules—such as scalar widening and extension, aggregate coercion or homogeneous-aggregate handling, register assignment and availability tracking, padding/alignment and varargs rules, ABI-variant selection, kernel or foreign-ABI special cases, and indirect passing/return decisions—so signatures are transformed into the concrete ABI required by targets including AArch64, AMDGPU, ARM, AVR, BPF, Hexagon, LoongArch, M68k, MIPS/MIPS64, MSP430, NVPTX64, PowerPC/PowerPC64, RISC-V, s390x, SPARC/SPARC64, WebAssembly, x86, x86-64 SysV, and x86-64 Win64.
